resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Spanish source scope, prior review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Spanish pass identified 25 actionable circuit, formal-register, geometry, thermal, SI, and wire-gauge defects; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Spanish human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The Kirchhoff description was vague about the conserved quantities.
evidence: The previous text referred generally to conservation at nodes and around loops.
findings.resolution: Named charge conservation at nodes and energy conservation in closed loops.

findings.summary: The current-law example used the awkward phrase conducir hacia fuera.
evidence: The previous sentence repeated hacia fuera and used an indirect branch construction.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it with deja salir, total, and resolver el circuito.

findings.summary: The series-resistor setup used a less direct passive construction.
evidence: The previous setup said the resistors in series were connected to 8 V.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Dos resistencias ... se conectan en serie a una fuente.

findings.summary: The KVL paragraph used less precise wording for voltage rises and drops.
evidence: The previous paragraph used aumentos and caídas without the more direct subidas y caídas phrasing.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the paragraph with subidas, caídas, bucle, polarities, and connected series components.

findings.summary: The series-cell capacity sentence was ambiguous about the retained cell capacity.
evidence: The previous sentence referred to an equivalent cell without specifying equal capacity.
findings.resolution: Clarified that the ampere-hour capacity matches a cell of equal capacity.

findings.summary: The parallel-cell sentence used celdas paralelas rather than the standard connection wording.
evidence: The previous sentence did not explicitly say connected in parallel.
findings.resolution: Changed it to celdas conectadas en paralelo.

findings.summary: The resistor relationship was phrased as voltage and current of the resistance.
evidence: The previous wording was less precise about voltage across a resistor.
findings.resolution: Changed it to relate the voltage in each resistor to its current through V = I × R.

findings.summary: The TCR description said the coefficient estimates rather than describes the resistance change.
evidence: The previous description used estima for the core definition.
findings.resolution: Changed it to describe how a material's resistance changes with temperature.

findings.summary: The constant-voltage TCR paragraph used accionada, which is unnatural for a resistor supply.
evidence: The previous text described a resistor as accionada a voltaje constante.
findings.resolution: Changed it to alimentada con tensión constante.

findings.summary: The cosine ratio retained English geometry labels.
evidence: The formula used adjacent and hypotenuse rather than Spanish labels.
findings.resolution: Changed it to adyacente / hipotenusa.

findings.summary: The tangent ratio retained English geometry labels.
evidence: The formula used opposite and adjacent rather than Spanish labels.
findings.resolution: Changed it to opuesto / adyacente.

findings.summary: The inverse-sine formula retained English geometry labels.
evidence: The formula used opposite and hypotenuse inside a Spanish presentation.
findings.resolution: Changed it to opuesto / hipotenusa.

findings.summary: The inverse-cosine formula retained English geometry labels.
evidence: The formula used adjacent and hypotenuse inside a Spanish presentation.
findings.resolution: Changed it to adyacente / hipotenusa.

findings.summary: The inverse-tangent formula retained English geometry labels.
evidence: The formula used opposite and adjacent inside a Spanish presentation.
findings.resolution: Changed it to opuesto / adyacente.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating heading was longer and less natural than the physical-process term.
evidence: The previous heading was Calentamiento con energía eléctrica.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Calentamiento eléctrico.

findings.summary: The electrical-heating example switched to informal tú while surrounding instructions use formal usted.
evidence: The setup began Calienta el ejemplo.
findings.resolution: Changed it to the formal Caliente el ejemplo.

findings.summary: The heat-flux description did not explicitly state per-unit-area transfer.
evidence: The previous description said heat crosses a surface without defining density per area.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as heat transfer rate per unit area.

findings.summary: The heat-flux example title omitted the density term.
evidence: The previous title was Flujo promedio del calentador.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Densidad de flujo térmico media del calentador.

findings.summary: The heat-flux conclusion named flujo de calor despite reporting W/m².
evidence: The units describe heat-flux density rather than total heat flow.
findings.resolution: Changed it to densidad de flujo térmico and retained both units.

findings.summary: The convection paragraph called h a surface coefficient.
evidence: The previous paragraph used coeficiente superficial h.
findings.resolution: Changed it to coeficiente de convección h.

findings.summary: The SI description was generic and omitted derived units and decimal prefixes.
evidence: The previous text only described a coherent basis for units and conversion.
findings.resolution: Named coherent base and derived units plus decimal prefixes for technical calculations.

findings.summary: The SI heading said common units rather than base units.
evidence: The heading did not distinguish the SI base-unit table from derived-unit bullets.
findings.resolution: Changed it to Unidades básicas del SI.

findings.summary: The decimal-prefix table retained English prefix names in a Spanish presentation.
evidence: The rows used English kilo, mega, milli, micro, and nano labels.
findings.resolution: Localized the five prefix names to kilo, mega, mili, micro, and nano.

findings.summary: The wire-gauge description did not explain that a number is system-dependent.
evidence: The previous description did not warn that the same number can map to different diameters.
findings.resolution: Clarified that a gauge number is nominal only when the gauge system is specified.

findings.summary: The AWG inch and millimetre formulas used decimal points in a comma-decimal Spanish locale.
evidence: The formulas contained 0.005 and 0.127 while the surrounding Spanish values use comma decimals.
findings.resolution: Changed the constants to 0,005 and 0,127.
